question.text: If $x y^{\prime}+y-e^x=0, y(a)=b$, then $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1} y(x)$ is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text {Hint : } \quad xy^{\prime}+y-e^x=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x \frac{d y}{d x}+y=e^x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x d y+y d x=e^x d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \int d(x y)=\int e^x d x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad x y=e^x+c \\ & \quad y(a)=b \Rightarrow c=a b-e^a \\ & \therefore \quad y(x)=\frac{e^x+a b-e^a}{x} \\ & \therefore \quad \lim _{x \rightarrow 1} y(x)=e+a b-e^a\end{aligned}$
